demand_source.title: Model failover: user-visible fallback notices (OpenClaw docs)
demand_source.supports: OpenClaw tells the person in a direct chat when another model has answered in place of the usual one and when the usual one is back, the same down-and-back pair of notices this card sends for an outage.

edits.description: When the cloud model has an incident, a parent who texts Happy today gets OpenClaw's own error line, which may be little more than the provider's status (its exact wording on iMessage has not been seen), and a scheduled brief is simply missed: the scheduler's own failure notice starts only after two failures in a row, and the jobs registry (G003) routes it to Tony, not the family. With this, when model errors go on for a set number of minutes, each parent gets one plain 'the model is down' line and later a 'back' line, and the alerts that need no model keep working: the weather watch, the stop phrase, and any fixed reminder Tony has set up as a no-model job (bin day). As an option Tony has to decide on, the vendor's lower-cost model answers that turn and the chat shows a one-line notice saying so; OpenClaw's security guidance warns against running an agent that has tools on a smaller model, so this part stays off unless he accepts that.
edits.example: Trigger: gpt-6-sol returns server errors at 07:00 while the morning brief is due, and the error alert stays on past the set number of minutes. Each parent gets one fixed line saying the model is down and that weather alerts and fixed reminders still arrive, and one 'back' line once it recovers; the 07:00 brief itself is missed.
caveats: OpenClaw's prompt-injection guidance says not to use smaller or cheaper model tiers for agents that have tools or read outside content, and each parent's main agent does both (reminders, lists, family delivery, photos and PDFs). The fallback here is the vendor's lower-cost model, so allowing it is a decision and not a default; without it an outage means the plain notice and no answers until the usual model is back.

OpenAI's status history listed 39 incidents in September 2026 and 23 in the first ten days of October across all its products. Most do not touch the API models Happy uses, but some did, for example 'elevated error rates across API models' on 17 Sep.
An answer from the smaller model can be worse than the usual one; the fallback notice tells the parent which model answered.
No fallback to a second vendor: it would need another vendor's key and a new privacy decision, and the local route is the skipped M2, so a vendor-wide outage still means no answers until it ends.
An API key that hits its monthly cap looks like an outage until the month ends; the fixed line should say 'limit reached' when that is the cause.
If the Mac, the home internet or iMessage is what failed, nothing here helps. The dead-man alert is then the only signal and it goes to Tony.

A scheduled brief that fails is simply missed unless the job's retry settings say otherwise. OpenClaw's scheduler already sends a failure notice after two failures in a row and one recovery notice afterwards, but the jobs registry (G003) routes those to Tony, so the line built here is the only word the family gets.

A parent who texts during an outage is not met with silence today: the failover page says a turn in which every model fails ends with a failure summary, such as a line that all models are temporarily rate-limited, with the time the cooldown ends when that is known. What this card adds is the unprompted line to both parents and the 'back' line.

demand_source.title: OpenClaw AGENTS.md template: be proactive
demand_source.supports: OpenClaw's own agent template tells a proactive agent to stay quiet at night and when nothing is new, and lets only an urgent item through.

edits.description: Caps how many unprompted texts each parent gets in a day, stops non-urgent ones outside allowed hours and labels each one so you know which job sent it. A text stopped by the cap or the hours is dropped, not sent later, so scheduled jobs are timed inside the allowed hours in the first place. Either parent can text 'mute until 3' or 'we are away next week', and briefs, bin reminders and routines pause for that window while urgent alerts still arrive. The pause is dependable only for a job that holds the household-store tool and checks the pause itself (the week-ahead and morning briefs as specified, and the evening brief once it is given that read), and best effort for timed reminders and any other job without the tool, which can only be stopped at delivery.
caveats: Each iPhone can already silence the night on a schedule, so what Happy adds is the daily cap, the urgent or not-urgent split, the label and the pause by chat.

The delivery hook can only rewrite or cancel a text, so one stopped by the daily cap or by quiet hours is dropped, not delivered later; holding texts and releasing them in a batch would need a queue of the plugin's own, which is not designed. Scheduled jobs are therefore timed inside the allowed hours, and the hook is the backstop.

It is not a hard gate for scheduled texts: the message_sending hook that sees `--announce` deliveries lets the message through if the plugin throws or times out, and only the agent's own message tool is gated fail-closed.
The reading of the announce path comes from bundled JavaScript and not a doc page, so confirm it with a throwaway hook before relying on either hook.
No doc lists a job id on message_sending, so each job may have to write its own tag into the text.
No built-in quiet hours or priority classes were found in OpenClaw, so keeping urgent alerts on during a mute depends on this plugin.
The household store does not exist yet, so the counters and the paused-until row are a design and not an installed feature.
The fixed emergency reply (CRT-13) answers an inbound text and must never be held back by quiet hours, caps or a mute.

Timed reminders run with an empty tool list (F007), so a reminder job cannot check the pause itself; its text is stopped only by the delivery hook, which is the best-effort side. A mute is therefore dependable for the briefs and other jobs that read the row themselves and best effort for reminders. Because a stopped text is dropped and not sent late, a one-off reminder that falls inside a mute would be lost, so one-off reminders a parent set belong in a class that passes; a recurring one such as the bins reminder can pause, because the next one comes round anyway.

Switching a job off by chat is open only to a command owner, which is Tony's handle alone today (adding Jordan is the open decision recorded on F007). OpenClaw's page gives that sender's agent the power to update, run or remove any job on the Gateway, not only to pause one, and a job changed that way no longer matches the registry (G003). The paused-until row is the route both parents use, and it changes no job.

The evening brief (F014) is specified with the weather and calendar tools only, so as written it cannot read the paused-until row. Give that job the household-store read as well, or its pause rests on the best-effort delivery hook, like a timed reminder's.

demand_source.title: Fambot: AI Family Assistant (App Store listing by Fambot Inc)
demand_source.supports: A shipping family assistant sells the same function: it reads school emails and newsletters and sends parents a daily digest of what to know, do and decide.

edits.description: A separate mailbox registered with school, PTA, coaches and the lunch system is read by an isolated, memory-less reader, so no parent's private inbox is touched. Weekday afternoons both parents get a five-line text of the day's school and activity mail with dates spelled out, a dated to-do list, and one line per child from the school platforms' own summary emails where the school uses them. A parent who wants a day-before reminder for a line asks their own agent for it. Attachments are not opened: a newsletter sent as a PDF or a picture shows up only as a file name.
edits.safety: All school mail is untrusted and is read only by the memory-less school-mail agent, which has no web or file tools and can only announce to the two parents. The sender allowlist with verified authentication is the mail plugin's check on its own per-message path; the 16:00 digest job reads the mailbox through a separate read-only tool that this check does not cover, so that job needs its own sender filter (see caveats). Links are relayed only when their domain matches the allowlisted sender. No agent logs in to a school portal and no portal credentials are stored.
caveats: Pick the mailbox provider with the password in mind: the plugin signs in with a mailbox password only, which on Gmail means a Google app password that Google does not recommend, while OpenClaw's guide names Fastmail and iCloud.

Each school system has to accept an extra guardian address, a manual chore per system, and auto-forwarding from a parent's Gmail may fail the plugin's aligned-DMARC check, so registering the address directly is the safe route.
The reader gets body text and attachment file names only, so PDF or image newsletters and flyer attachments are not read.

Urgent alerts are not this digest's job, since the school's own alerts reach the parents' phones first; the reader keeps one backup rule (a closure, delay or early-dismissal message from an allowlisted school sender is passed on at the next sweep, not held until 16:00), and sorting urgent from routine on real district mail is untested.

PowerSchool emails carry grades and attendance and Classroom summaries carry assignment titles: these are a child's education records and they reach the cloud model under store:false, which is why the card is rated medium risk.
Classroom summaries (missing and upcoming work, no grades) arrive only if the school uses Classroom and the teacher switches them on, and the guardian invitation expires after 120 days.
One job appears to take one delivery target, so two parents need two jobs or the parents' group chat, and the iCloud read path likely needs an in-house himalaya wrapper.

For a school or team app that sends no email, try the app's own email notifications into this mailbox first and a parent's screenshot to Happy second; Canvas and ClassDojo have no verified email path.

The reminder step is not wired end to end. The reader that writes the digest holds no reminder or store tool, on purpose, because it reads untrusted mail, and it is untested whether the parent's own agent, which receives any reply, can see the digest text. Until that is tested, a parent names the line when asking their own agent for a reminder. Giving the reader a write to the household store would let text from a school email reach the parents' private agents, so that route needs its own review first.

The sender list lives in family.json5 and changes only with a reviewed deploy, so a parent who needs a new coach or teacher added asks Tony. The mail plugin logs a rejected message without its subject or body, so a mail that did not show up can be traced in the gateway log.
A calendar link that a school platform offers is subscribed in the family calendar (F009), not read by this reader.

The sender check with verified authentication runs only on the mail plugin's per-message path. The 16:00 digest job reads the mailbox itself through the read-only mail tool, so mail from a sender who is not on the list (spam, a faked address) would reach the reader unless the job filters by sender or the digest is built only from what the plugin let in. The reader holds nothing but the mailbox read and can only text the two parents, which limits the harm to a misleading digest line. Which of the two routes builds the digest is not settled.
unverified: Whether the district, PTA, coaches and lunch system each accept an extra or shared guardian address; this is a manual chore per system.

Auto-forwarding school mail from a parent's Gmail by filter may fail the plugin's aligned-DMARC check (Google's forwarding guidance says forwarded mail often fails SPF); DKIM survival was not tested, so registering the address directly is the safe route.
An iCloud+ custom-domain address with this plugin was not tested; Apple documents the IMAP host and app-specific passwords, not this combination.

Whether himalaya has an MCP mode; its README does not mention one, so the iCloud path likely needs an in-house wrapper. The README also says native keyring support was removed in v2, so its password comes from a command.
That one job takes exactly one delivery target (hence two jobs or one group chat for two parents); I saw single-target examples only.
Groups are off today, so a family group chat target needs the iMessage group allowlist switched on first.
Which platforms this family's district uses, and each platform's exact sender address and authentication result.
Whether the school uses Google Classroom at all, and whether a student can have the school mailbox as an extra guardian next to both parents.
ClassDojo's notification behaviour and Canvas's calendar feed for observers; neither page could be opened.
Whether a parent's reply to the digest reaches an agent that can see the digest text: the digest is announced by the school-mail agent from an isolated run, and replies go to the parent's own agent.

What the mail plugin's `deliver` switch does when it is on: the account settings have the switch (off by default) but no recipient field, so where a reader's summary would go is not documented on the page read.

demand_source.title: Keeping Track of Records | Childhood Vaccines | CDC
demand_source.supports: CDC tells parents that sports teams, summer camps and schools may ask for vaccination records, to keep them in a safe place, and that copies come from the doctor, the state registry or the school.

edits.how:
One Markdown page per child in the shared family folder, indexed through memory.search.extraPaths (F043 step 1). For each document it records where the official copy lives (the pediatric office, the state immunization registry, the filing cabinet), the date on it, and the date it stops being accepted. CDC says it holds no vaccination records and points parents to the child's doctor, the state immunization information system and the school, so the page notes which of those worked last time. A dated row per form in the household store (F031) is the checklist behind 'what do I still need?'; the warning two weeks before a form is due is a timed reminder (F007) offered through the dates-after-a-yes flow (F010), not a separate job. The date a physical or a record stops being accepted is also listed in the renewals look-ahead (F063), so that 'the physical on file is older than this camp accepts, book a visit' comes from the one list of things running out. The copy-paste block is drafted on

-main from a per-child 'form facts' section of the same page when the form arrives as a photo or PDF (F002), under a drafts-only rule in AGENTS.md; the agent has no exec, so it cannot alter or fill in the original form, and ID and policy numbers are left blank for the parent. Scans stay in Files or the paper folder; only the index and the form facts go to Happy.
caveats: Requirements differ by state, district and camp. Happy tracks what each form asked for last time; it does not know the rules.
The official immunization record has to come from the doctor or the state registry. Happy cannot fetch it, because portal logins are out of scope.
Signing is done by the parent, with the phone's markup tools or on paper. Happy never signs, fills a web form or submits.
An index of where documents are is itself sensitive. Keep ID numbers, policy numbers and certificate numbers out of it.
The form-facts section holds the children's health facts (allergies, medicines, conditions), and they reach the cloud model whenever an answer block is drafted.
The drafts-only rule is a prompt instruction; it holds only because the agent has no tool that could fill in or send a form.

Expiry dates overlap the renewals look-ahead (F063), which already carries a yearly well-visit nudge per child. Keep one list of what is running out there, and keep only the document index, form due dates and the paste-ready answers here.

A form's due date is the kind of date the dates-after-a-yes flow (F010) already turns into a reminder once the parent agrees. Use that flow and timed reminders (F007) for the warning; the household-store row here is the checklist behind 'what do I still need?', not a second reminder mechanism.

demand_source.title: Schedule actions in Gemini Apps - Gemini Apps Help
demand_source.supports: Google ships scheduled daily digests of a person's calendar, to-do list and email to prepare for the day ahead, the same kind of recurring logistics text.

edits.description: Each parent gets short scheduled texts built from the family calendar and the weather. Sunday to Thursday at 19:30: tomorrow's events, who drives, what to pack and the weather, and nothing when the day is unremarkable. Sunday at 18:00: the week ahead, with early releases, activities, drivers, packing, the weather outlook and open school deadlines. Optionally, weekdays at 07:00: weather and alerts, today's calendar, items due and trash day. Mail stays in its own digests: the school digest (F051) and each parent's 07:00 mail digest (part of G015).
caveats: On Sundays the 18:00 week-ahead and the 19:30 evening brief would both arrive within ninety minutes. Either let the Sunday week-ahead carry Monday's detail and run the evening brief Monday to Thursday only (`1-4`), or accept two texts.

The morning leg is the optional one: it needs the household store (F031) for items due and trash day, and the weather plugin returns no sunset, so a sunset line, if wanted, needs a small local calculation.

If the optional 07:00 morning brief and the morning mail digest (part of G015) are both switched on, a parent gets two texts at 07:00. They cannot be one job, because the mail agent and the parent's main agent are kept apart; move one of them by a quarter of an hour, or leave the morning brief off for a parent who has the mail digest.

Dates taken from mail are not part of the first build: they would come from a separate job on the mail agent (G015, wave C), and how that job hands dates to the brief without passing email text into the parent's main agent still has to be designed. Until then the school deadlines in the week-ahead are rows a parent typed or confirmed (F010).
The National Weather Service forecast reaches seven days ahead, so the Sunday 18:00 weather outlook covers the coming week and no further.

Google's Gemini app can already send a scheduled daily digest of a person's own Google calendar, to-do list and email (being rolled out gradually to personal accounts, up to ten active actions). What Happy's brief adds is the family's own layer: who drives, what to pack from the routines table, the forecast for home, silence on an unremarkable day, and arrival in the iMessage thread.

A mute or a vacation pause (G001) is dependable only for a job that reads the paused-until row in the household store before it writes. The week-ahead and morning legs hold that tool; the evening brief as specified does not, so either add the store read to its tool list or accept that its pause rests on G001's best-effort delivery hook.
